directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. eldredge_john_w, Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 — n1844_e0564 (a single entry).

Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. The value is the volume's own line, split by its crosswalk on the entry's punctuation. These volumes set the trade first and its qualifiers after it on the same line, so the split may carry an employer, a market or a corner along with the trade. The printed entry is quoted beside the value for exactly that reason: the split is checkable against it, and neither is read into an 1835 claim.

back_projection.note: REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE RECORD. Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 prints an address against this name in 1844 and this pass will not carry it back to 1835. The 1835 record prints no trade for this person, so there is no 1835 business for a later door to position. Minting one out of a directory printed after the scene date is the one thing this pass may never do. A refusal is written here rather than dropped so that a later run can see the address was read and ruled on, not missed (docs/ADDRESS-BACK-PROJECTION.md, clause 1).

residence_back_projection.note: A LATER HOME ADDRESS, READ BACKWARDS 9 YEARS. The street is not an 1835 reading: Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 printed where this person lived in 1844, and this pass carries it back to the scene date because nothing in the 1835 corpus says where the house stood. What is claimed is the street FACE and nothing narrower — no lot, no roof, no door count, and no corner even where the volume prints one — and the grade is `reconstructed`, this dataset's word for a figure the reconstruction supplies rather than a source. Randolph Street stands in 1835 under that name and in that place, and the entry prints it as this person's home. The volume narrows it further — it names Clark Street — and clause R5 declines to take the point: a corner or a run between two crossings is a fact about the numbered grid of the 1840s, and a house moves more than a shopfront does. So the placement is the FACE and nothing narrower, and no roof is dealt. A home is carried back on a weaker argument than a shop is: a shopfront is capital sunk into one street's trade and a lodging is a month's rent, which is why this policy claims less than docs/ADDRESS-BACK-PROJECTION.md does from the same volume. The rule is docs/RESIDENCE-BACK-PROJECTION.md and the liberty is L223; a reader who thinks 9 years is too far to carry a house should read the grade as the disagreement being invited.
